item.title: State Attorneys General Push for Data Protections as Character.AI Files for Bankruptcy
item.description:
State Attorneys General Push for Data Protections as Character.AI Files for Bankruptcy

Character.AI announced on Tuesday that it is filing for Chapter 11 bankruptcy and is selling some assets to Disney. The filing triggered a multi‑state investigation led by New York Attorney General Letitia James, who, together with 39 other bipartisan attorneys general, is seeking safeguards for the company’s user data.

🔍 Overview

  • Character.AI filed for Chapter 11 and disclosed that several states were mid‑investigation when the bankruptcy filing occurred.
  • The investigation began in 2024 after a lawsuit from the mother of a 14‑year‑old who died by suicide allegedly seconds after talking with the chatbot.
  • The AGs describe the findings as “exceptionally serious dangers” and “potentially unlawful conduct.”

⚖️ Legal Actions

  • Letitia James revealed a years‑long multi‑state probe into Character.AI’s consumer‑data practices.
  • James is among 40 bipartisan AGs who filed a notice of interest in the bankruptcy case “to put all parties on notice of the regulatory issues that will need to be addressed in any sale or transfer of the Debtor’s business or assets.”
  • The states are urging the bankruptcy judge to require the purchaser of Character.AI’s assets to implement specific data‑protection procedures.

📊 Consumer Risks Highlighted by the Investigation

  • Highly sensitive conversations users have with chatbot characters.
  • Large number of minors using the product.
  • Chatbots posing as licensed professionals.
  • Exposure to sexual and violent content.
  • Weak age‑verification checks.
  • Misleading safety claims.
  • Potential violations of state privacy laws.

🛡️ Proposed Safeguards for Any Buyer

  • Effective age‑assurance systems.
  • Restrictions on how minors can engage with the chatbots.
  • Implementation of “Crisis safeguards.”
  • Mechanisms that let users delete their data.

The AGs warn that without such protections, “this company collected some of the most private thoughts children have ever shared, and now those conversations could be sold off to the highest bidder.” James said, “I am fighting to make sure any buyer puts children’s safety first and puts real protections in place.”

Character.AI and Disney have not responded to requests for comment.

#CharacterAI #DataPrivacy #Bankruptcy

Source: Now that Character.AI is going bankrupt, what happens to all of its users’ data?

item.title: Character.AI files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy and seeks sale of assets to Disney
item.description:
Character.AI files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy and seeks sale of assets to Disney

Character.AI, an early generative‑AI chatbot startup, announced on Monday that it has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the United States and is pursuing a sale of its assets to Disney.

🔍 Overview

  • The company filed for bankruptcy to facilitate the sale of the business and its assets.
  • Disney is positioned as the lead bidder, offering $20 million for certain undisclosed assets and a non‑exclusive license to unspecified intellectual property.
  • The sale includes transition support using former Character.AI employees hired by Disney.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Estimated liabilities are listed between $50 million and $100 million.
  • Disney would also receive a non‑exclusive license to the company’s intellectual property.
  • The company expects the sale process to close late November or early December.
  • Character.AI will keep its services, including paid subscriptions, running while the sale proceeds.
  • The platform will be wound down if a suitable bid does not emerge.
  • The company emphasized that “maintaining a safe and engaging experience for our community remains a top priority.”

👥 Leadership Change

  • Disney hired former Character.AI CEO Karandeep Anand as its chief technology officer.
  • Anand’s tenure as CEO lasted just over a year, during which he oversaw the move into microdramas.
  • Disney also expects “a number of Character.AI’s technical team” to join the company.

📚 Legal & Safety Challenges

  • Character.AI has faced mounting scrutiny and lawsuits over the safety of its chatbots.
  • Disney previously sent cease‑and‑desist letters, claiming Character.AI was damaging its brand and exploiting Disney intellectual property by allowing unauthorized chatbots of Disney characters.

🔄 Acquisition Strategy

  • The deal resembles an “acquihire” approach, where the buyer primarily seeks talent.
  • Character.AI previously survived a similar talent‑acquisition when Google spent over $2 billion in 2024 to hire much of the company’s team, including co‑founders Noam Shazeer and Daniel De Freitas.

📅 Timeline & Next Steps

  • Bankruptcy filing and press release were published on Monday (date not specified).
  • Sale process expected to complete late November or early December.
  • Services will continue operating, with paid subscriptions remaining active, unless no suitable bid is received.
  • Disney’s involvement includes payment, licensing, and transition support using former staff.

#CharacterAI #DisneyAI #Bankruptcy #AcquiHire
